title: QPortfolio Scenario Data
description: Root document for a QPortfolio scenario file (qp_file_type = "QPortfolio Scenario Data"). A scenario is one "what-if" case within a portfolio: its settings, optimization configuration, metric limits, the selected opportunities, and any selection rules overridden from the portfolio defaults. All opportunity and metric names must match those defined in the portfolio.

metadata.description: Document header. For a scenario file qp_file_type must be "QPortfolio Scenario Data".

qp_file_type.description: Discriminator for the document type: "QPortfolio Data" for a portfolio data file, "QPortfolio Scenario Data" for a scenario file, "QPortfolio Model" for a model file and "QPortfolio Bundle" for a bundle manifest. Required.

qp_version.description: Version of the QPortfolio application that wrote this file, e.g. 4.6. Optional; when omitted the importer assumes the current version. A version newer than the importing application's is refused.

settings.description: Scenario identity and case settings (name, colour, data version, characteristics).

scenario_name.description: Human-readable name of the scenario. On import, a name already taken in the portfolio gets " (n)" appended.

color.description: Display colour for the scenario as a hex string, e.g. "#C25A38". Optional; unset, the scenario reads back with a generated colour.

description.description: Free-text description of the scenario. Optional.

instance_selection_threshold.description: Opportunity Instance Selection Threshold: the lowest fractional interest (between 0 and 1) counted as one instance when the opportunity is selected. Interests below it count as zero instances. Should be greater than the optimization feasibility_tolerance; not enforced. Optional; unset counts as the system threshold 0.000001.

enable_soft_constraints.description: When true, soft metric limits are allowed to be violated for a penalty in this scenario. Optional; defaults to false.

save_infeasible_run.description: When true, an optimization run that ends infeasible is still saved on the scenario. Optional; omitted means false.

data_version_name.description: Name of the data version this scenario loads for calculation/optimization (the input/master data set used).

characteristics.description: Scenario-level attribute/characteristic selections (e.g. a price set), driving sensitivity without changing opportunity inputs. Optional. One characteristic per attribute.

items.description: A single attribute/value pair, e.g. attribute = "Country", value = "Canada".

value.description: The characteristic value for this attribute. Null/absent means unset. A Date attribute's value is an Excel serial-date number as text, e.g. "45322" = 2024-01-31; a Numeric attribute's is a plain number as text.

optimization.description: Optimization configuration: the objective metric and direction plus solver settings.

direction.description: Whether to maximize or minimize the objective metric. Allowed values: `Maximize` — Maximize the objective metric (e.g. maximize NPV).; `Minimize` — Minimize the objective metric (e.g. minimize spend)..

objective_metric_name.description: Name of the metric to optimize (the objective function), e.g. an NPV metric. The metric must be neither hidden nor report-only.

objective_time_period.description: For a time-series objective, the one period (time-step, 0-based: 0 is the portfolio's first period) whose metric value is optimized - that period alone, not a total up to it. Optional for scalar objective metric. Must be less than the portfolio's total period count. Unset counts as 0 (the first period).

feasibility_tolerance.description: Feasibility tolerance: how strictly constraints must be honoured. A plain number with no unit, greater than 0. Default ~1E-7. Should be smaller than the instance_selection_threshold; not enforced. Optional.

optimality_tolerance.description: Optimality tolerance: tolerance on the nonlinear solver's rate-of-improvement test. A plain number with no unit, greater than 0. Default ~1E-4. Optional.

optimality_gap_absolute.description: Absolute optimality gap: stop once the gap between the objective value and the best bound is within this absolute amount, in the objective metric's own units. 0 or more. Optional.

optimality_gap_percentage.description: Relative optimality gap (percent): stop once the objective value is within this percentage of the best bound. A percent from 0 to 100, so 1 means 1 %, not 0.01. Optional.

penalty_weight.description: Overall scenario soft-constraints penalty weight applied across all soft metric limits. A plain weight with no unit, greater than 0. Optional; unset counts as 10000000 (1e7).

progress_interval.description: Solver progress check interval, in seconds: how often optimization status is updated. At least 1. Optional; unset counts as 10.

timeout_minutes.description: Maximum minutes the solver may search. At least 1. Default 1. Optional.

enforce_timeout.description: When true, stop all solver sub-problems at once on timeout rather than letting each honour its own timeout. Optional; defaults to false.

load_selections.description: When true, load the scenario's current selections as the solver's starting point. Optional; defaults to false.

use_linearization.description: When true, replace nonlinear operations with equivalent linear ones (see linearization_level). Optional; defaults to true.

linearization_level.description: Which functions to linearize when use_linearization is true. Optional; defaults to SolverDecide. Allowed values: `SolverDecide` — Let the solver decide which functions to linearize.; `AbsMinMax` — Linearize the ABS, MAX and MIN functions only.; `All` — Linearize all supported functions..

use_local_solver.description: When true, use local solver(s) instead of the default global solver. Optional; defaults to false.

max_local_solver.description: Number of local solvers to run (up to 100) when use_local_solver is true. Optional; unset counts as 1.

quadratic_xor_dependency.description: When true, model 'must not' selection dependencies with a quadratic expression (a*b = 0) instead of a Lindo Special Ordered Set. Optional; unset, the installation's setting applies, false unless an administrator changes it.

strict_selection_threshold.description: When true, strictly enforce the instance_selection_threshold by overriding the feasibility tolerance. Optional; unset, the installation's setting applies, false unless an administrator changes it.

solver_parameters.description: Expert Lindo solver parameters (id/value pairs). For advanced tuning; refer to Lindo documentation. Optional.

items.description: An expert Lindo solver parameter as an id/value pair.

id.description: Lindo parameter id. Must be an id the application's Lindo solver supports.

metric_limits.description: Metric limits/targets the optimizer must honour for this scenario (per-metric, per-period).

items.description: A limit or target placed on a metric's scenario value (per period; for a Group-level metric, the sum over its groups) that the optimizer must honour. A limit may be made soft to allow violation for a penalty.

disabled.description: When true the limit is present but ignored by the optimizer. Optional; defaults to false.

metric_name.description: Name of the metric being limited. Must match a model metric name, and the metric must be neither hidden nor report-only.

limit_type.description: Whether targets are a minimum (lower bound) or maximum (upper bound). Allowed values: `Minimum` — The metric value must be at least the target (lower bound).; `Maximum` — The metric value must be at most the target (upper bound)..

unit.description: The limit's own unit label for its targets, e.g. "$ MM", saved with the limit: a later change to the metric's unit does not change it. When given, it must equal the metric's unit. Missing or null: the metric's current unit is saved; "" = no unit.

targets.description: The per-period target values for the metric's scenario value (for a Group-level metric, the sum over its groups, not each group). Periods not listed are unconstrained for this metric. For a scalar metric only the period 0 target is kept.

items.description: A single per-period target value for a metric limit.

period.description: Time period this target applies to (0-based). A period at or past the portfolio's total period count, selection_time_period_count + input_time_period_count - 1, is stored but not used.

value.description: The target value the metric is bounded to in this period (interpreted as a minimum or maximum per the limit's limit_type).

disabled.description: When true this period's target is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

soft.description: When true this limit may be violated for a penalty (a soft constraint) rather than being strictly enforced. Requires the scenario's enable_soft_constraints. Optional; defaults to false.

magnitude.description: For a soft limit, the magnitude (scale of allowed violation) used in the penalty calculation. Optional; applies only when soft is true. Unset, it is estimated from the limit's targets.

penalty_weight.description: For a soft limit, the penalty weight applied to violations of this limit against the objective; higher weights make the limit 'harder'. Optional; unset counts as 50. Applies only when soft is true.

opportunity_selections.description: The selected quantity of each opportunity by period — the optimization result or a manually edited set of selections.

items.description: The selected quantity of one opportunity across periods.

opportunity_name.description: Name of the selected opportunity. Must match a defined opportunity.

selections.description: The per-period selection values. An empty list means the opportunity is not selected in any period.

items.description: The selected quantity of an opportunity in a single period.

period.description: Time period of the selection (0-based). A period at or past the portfolio's selection_time_period_count is stored but not used.

value.description: Selected quantity (interest) for this period. 1 = a full selection; a fraction (e.g. 0.5) = a partial selection where allowed; 0 = not selected.

selection_constraints.description: Selection constraints overridden for this scenario if present(not null) (otherwise inherited from the portfolio).

items.description: Selection limits scoped to one named opportunity.

opportunity_name.description: Unique name of the opportunity these limits apply to.

disabled.description: When true the constraint is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

integer_only.description: When true the optimizer may only make whole (integer) selections of this unit — no partial/fractional selection.

interior_limit.description: Min Fraction: the minimum quantity that must be selected IF the unit is selected (it does not force selection). Applies per instance and only when non-integer selection is allowed; ignored when integer_only is true. Optional.

total_minimum.description: Minimum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). A positive value forces selection.

total_maximum.description: Maximum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). 0 forbids selection.

total_instances_minimum.description: Minimum number of instances (each in-period selection counts as one instance regardless of fractional size; 1.1 counts as two). A positive value forces selection. Optional.

total_instances_maximum.description: Maximum number of instances allowed. Optional.

time_period_minima.description: Per-period minimum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). A positive entry forces selection in that period. May be empty (no per-period minima) or shorter than the horizon (unspecified periods are unbounded below). Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.

time_period_maxima.description: Per-period maximum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). Caps selection in that period, and 0 forbids it. Periods past the end of the array are capped at 0 as well, so an empty array forbids selection in every period - give a positive value for each period the opportunity may be selected in. An entry below the matching time_period_minima is accepted and surfaces as a selection constraint conflict. Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.

selection_dependency.description: Selection dependencies overridden for this scenario if present(not null) (otherwise inherited from the portfolio).

items.description: One selection-dependency rule. Read as: for the dependent opportunity to be selected, the independent opportunity must/must-not be selected, within the range that timing (before/after/during) and timing_offset set relative to the dependent's selected period, in the given quantity ratio.

xid.description: The rule's identifier, assigned by the product, e.g. sd-271679; cannot be set or changed.

disabled.description: When true the rule is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

dependent_opportunity.description: Name of the dependent opportunity — the one whose selection triggers the rule ("to select X…"). X is the dependent.

independent_opportunity.description: Name of the independent opportunity the dependent's selection depends on.

type.description: Whether the independent opportunity must, or must not, be selected. Allowed values: `Must` — The independent opportunity MUST be selected for the dependent to be selected.; `MustNot` — The independent opportunity MUST NOT be selected when the dependent is selected (an exclusive either/or condition). A MustNot rule carries no ratio: each_scale omitted, each_interest false, need_scale 1, need_interest false..

timing.description: Range direction of the timing relationship (over-all / before / after / during). Allowed values: `OverAll` — The relationship applies across all periods (no directional timing).; `Before` — The independent selection must occur at or before the dependent's period plus timing_offset.; `After` — The independent selection must occur at or after the dependent's period plus timing_offset.; `During` — The independent selection must occur exactly in the dependent's period plus timing_offset..

timing_offset.description: Signed number of periods that moves the boundary of the constrained range away from the dependent's selected period t: Before = independent at or before t + offset, After = independent at or after t + offset, During = independent exactly at t + offset. The sign does not encode direction (that is the timing field). Example: "B at least 8 periods after A" is dependent B, independent A, Must, Before, -8. After with +8 and the same roles is the reverse rule (A at least 8 periods after B).

each_scale.description: Ratio scale on the dependent side ('each' clause). With each_interest, expresses the dependent quantity in the 'N instances / R selections' ratio. Optional; unset means no limit on the dependent quantity (any number).

each_interest.description: When true the 'each' ratio is expressed in real-number selections (R, interest); when false it is expressed in instance counts (N).

need_scale.description: Ratio scale on the independent side ('need' clause), paired with need_interest.

need_interest.description: When true the 'need' ratio is expressed in real-number selections (R, interest); when false it is expressed in instance counts (N).

selection_group.description: Selection groups overridden for this scenario if present(not null) (otherwise inherited from the portfolio).

groups.description: The selection groups and their members.

items.description: One selection group: a named set of member opportunities linked by the group type.

disabled.description: When true the group is present but its linking behaviour is ignored (members fall back to their individual constraints). Optional; defaults to false.

group_name.description: Unique name of the group. Referenced by group_limits.group_name.

type.description: Whether membership is mutually inclusive or mutually exclusive. Allowed values: `MutualInclusive` — Mutually inclusive: all members are selected if any member is selected, in the same period as the triggering member.; `MutualExclusive` — Mutually exclusive: only one member may be selected; the others are excluded and remain unavailable in later periods..

members.description: The member opportunities of this group.

items.description: One member of a selection group.

opportunity_name.description: Name of the member opportunity. Must match a defined opportunity.

disabled.description: When true this membership is removed from the group and the opportunity's own selection constraints re-apply. Optional; a new membership is enabled.

group_limits.description: Group-level selection limits, one per group, keyed by group_name. While a group's limits are active they take precedence over members' individual selection constraints.

items.description: Group-level selection limits applied to all members of one group. Inherits the same min/max/instance/per-period bounds as an opportunity limit; a group Max applies to each member (e.g. Max = 2 means each selected member may be selected up to twice), not to the count of members chosen.

group_name.description: Name of the group these limits apply to. Must match a group's group_name.

disabled.description: When true the constraint is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

integer_only.description: When true the optimizer may only make whole (integer) selections of this unit — no partial/fractional selection.

interior_limit.description: Min Fraction: the minimum quantity that must be selected IF the unit is selected (it does not force selection). Applies per instance and only when non-integer selection is allowed; ignored when integer_only is true. Optional.

total_minimum.description: Minimum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). A positive value forces selection.

total_maximum.description: Maximum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). 0 forbids selection.

total_instances_minimum.description: Minimum number of instances (each in-period selection counts as one instance regardless of fractional size; 1.1 counts as two). A positive value forces selection. Optional.

total_instances_maximum.description: Maximum number of instances allowed. Optional.

time_period_minima.description: Per-period minimum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). A positive entry forces selection in that period. May be empty (no per-period minima) or shorter than the horizon (unspecified periods are unbounded below). Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.

time_period_maxima.description: Per-period maximum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). Caps selection in that period, and 0 forbids it. Periods past the end of the array are capped at 0 as well, so an empty array forbids selection in every period - give a positive value for each period the opportunity may be selected in. An entry below the matching time_period_minima is accepted and surfaces as a selection constraint conflict. Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.
